title: CAMPED AT GILGAL, STONES SET UP

memory_verse.label: Bible Reference
memory_verse.text: On the tenth day of the first month the people went up from the Jordan and camped at Gilgal on the eastern border of Jericho. And Joshua set up at Gilgal the twelve stones they had taken out of the Jordan. — Josh 4:19-20 (NIV)

devotion.label: Devotion
devotion.text:
The people arrive at Gilgal and Joshua sets up the twelve memorial stones there. Notice the precise date recorded: "the tenth day of the first month." God's works happen in real time and space, at actual dates and places. Our faith is not built on vague legends but on things that truly happened, that could be dated and located and pointed to.

Gilgal would become an important place for Israel — a base camp, a place of renewal and remembrance. And at its heart stood these twelve stones, a permanent reminder of the day God brought them across the Jordan. Every time they returned to Gilgal, the stones would preach again: God is faithful. God made a way.

There is wisdom in having a place and a marker that anchors our memory of God's goodness. Life moves fast, and gratitude fades. A visible reminder helps us return again and again to the truth of what God has done.

Our faith, too, rests on real events in history — supremely the death and resurrection of Christ, which happened at a real place, in real time, witnessed by real people (1 Cor 15:3-6). We do not follow clever stories but a Saviour who truly rose. Let us set up our own "stones" of remembrance, returning often to the solid ground of what God has actually done.

reflection.label: Reflection
reflection.text:
1. Do you have "markers" — places, journals, habits — that anchor your memory of God's faithfulness?
2. How does it strengthen you that our faith rests on real, historical events?
3. What has God done in your life that you want to keep returning to and remembering?

prayer.label: Prayer
prayer.text: Lord, thank You that Your works are real and lasting, not vague ideas. Help me build reminders that keep me returning to Your faithfulness. Amen.
